rationale: C14 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both are letters installing or recruiting an administrator immediately after a statutory reorganization, then defining the office’s administrative mission and emphasizing procurement-related responsibilities and protection of small business. The child adapts C14’s General Services context to the Reconstruction Finance Corporation and adds Symington-specific qualifications and mobilization priorities. C09 and C20 share the personnel-letter pattern of matching experience to a new or continuing office, but neither has C14’s combination of statutory transition, administrator responsibilities, procurement, and small-business policy.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Senate action last week assures that the provisions of Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1951 regarding the Reconstruction Finance Corporation will become effective April thirtieth. I am writing at this time to ask you to accept the position of Administrator
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have today signed H.R. 4754... Pursuant to the authority of the new Act, I hereby designate you to perform temporarily... the functions of that officer, with the title of "Acting Administrator of General Services."
shared_material.explanation: Both letters begin with newly effective legislation or reorganization and immediately use it as the basis for placing the recipient in an administrator role.

shared_material.child_excerpt: your broad experience in private business and government is needed to provide the effective and efficient administration necessary to handle the important responsibilities of the RFC
shared_material.parent_excerpt: An important responsibility is vested in the Administrator of General Services to achieve effective and economical results in the property management field
shared_material.explanation: The child closely parallels the parent’s framing of the administrator’s office as carrying important responsibilities requiring effective administration.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Your experience... with respect to government procurement and disposal programs gives you special qualification for this phase of the work.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949 consolidates functions... [of] procurement, utilization, and disposal of Government property
shared_material.explanation: Both identify procurement and disposal functions as a central part of the administrator’s work.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I want to continue the policy of making the RFC program an effective part of our efforts to assist the growth and development of small business
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Act requires that a fair proportion of all procurement shall be placed with small business concerns... [and calls for] detailed standards... to insure a fair and substantial proportion of contract placement with small business establishments.
shared_material.explanation: Both close their substantive instructions by making support for small business an explicit policy obligation of the administrator.
